findings.reason: two nodes built from §5 and §8 will implement contradictory behaviour for one request class and one will fail the other's done-when, so §5's second sentence must be revised to defer to §8 (idle only when the service may not queue the upstream) or §8 must carve out §5's class.
findings.text: §8 queues the upstream when "a stored request waits on a section that is declared implementable, has no live request, and sits in a plan the service may queue", while §5 line 74 states that "a request waiting on a section nobody is building, whose upstream could still land, keeps the idle report it has today"; that is the same class of request, so one section queues it and the other leaves it idle, and the new §8 does not declare any reconciliation with §5

findings.reason: this is a soft performance target that does not alter what the section delivers or gate its functional arms; a node can still measure a pass-time delta, so naming a base would sharpen it but does not change the plan.
findings.text: §7's done-when closes with "On the fleet node, one pass over the mounted projects adds under two seconds to the pass", a timing bound stated with no base revision, comparator or sample size, so it sits beside the functional arms without a way to fail deterministically and would need its own uncontrolled benchmark
